articles.title: Todd Bowles' frustration with Jamel Dean paves way for stunning return by Shilo Sanders
articles.standfirst: Former Buccaneers safety joked he's still available after Bowles revisited a defensive assignment
articles.summary: Former Buccaneers safety joked he's still available after Bowles revisited a defensive assignment
articles.body:
Shilo Sanders has spent months sounding increasingly comfortable with the idea that his NFL career is over. That didn't stop him from taking a playful shot at getting back into Todd Bowles ’ defense.

The former Tampa Bay Buccaneers safety surfaced in the comments after Bowles told a story about cornerback Jamel Dean repeatedly struggling with a corner blitz assignment.

Bowles recalled reaching the point where he effectively stopped trusting Dean with the call.

“Dean messed up the corner blitz so much that I literally told him in practice, ‘Whenever I call this to the boundary, you go to the field from the other corner over the side. I said, You will never, ever,’” Bowles said.

“And then, his last year here, he ended up getting a sack, and I was laughing so hard. It was like the biggest moment of his life. … It took me six years to get him to get that right.”

Sanders couldn't resist: “I’ll blitz coach 😁,” he wrote. The comment reads more like a joke than an actual campaign for a roster spot, but it stood out because Sanders has recently spoken about football in much more final terms.

NFL opportunity ended on a costly mistake

Sanders joined Tampa Bay as an undrafted free agent in 2025 after finishing his college career at Colorado.

His chances of making the roster were always going to depend heavily on preseason performance and special teams value, but Bowles saw traits he liked during camp.

The coach described Sanders as having a “hunger” and called him “very aggressive.”

That opportunity disappeared during Tampa Bay’s third preseason game.

Sanders became involved in a confrontation with tight end Zach Davidson and threw a punch, resulting in an ejection. Bowles was blunt afterward.

“You can’t throw punches in this league... that’s inexcusable,” he said. “They’re going to get you every time. You’ve got to grow from that.”

The Buccaneers later released Sanders , and he hasn't found another NFL home since. His tone this year suggested he had stopped expecting one.

“I don’t think there’s any light in my tunnel,” Sanders said during a livestream.

He also characterized the end of his football career as a “blessing” while discussing the turbulent career path of former NFL star Antonio Brown .

“He be tweaking,” Sanders said.

Life after football already taking shape

Sanders has increasingly shifted his attention toward entertainment instead of a comeback.

He released a 15-track hip-hop album titled Hate 2 Love on Jan. 1 and has said he no longer trains with an NFL return as his primary goal.

“I’ve always done that my whole life playing football with music, acting, and modeling,” Sanders said. “I truly believe God has a big plan for me.”

He is also currently dealing with a bankruptcy case connected to an $11.89 million civil judgment involving former school security guard John Darjean .

Sanders has disputed the underlying account of the confrontation, while the current proceedings center on whether the debt can be discharged.

Against that backdrop, one Instagram comment is hardly evidence of a serious comeback attempt.

Still, Sanders ’ response to Bowles offered a revealing glimpse of where he stands.

He may believe the NFL chapter is finished, but apparently he is not completely opposed to answering the call if Tampa Bay ever needs an extra blitzer.

articles.title: Baker Mayfield injury update: Todd Bowles provides more details on his thumb injury
articles.standfirst: Mayfield picked up the injury in action against the Minnesota Vikings.
articles.summary: Mayfield picked up the injury in action against the Minnesota Vikings.
articles.body:
B aker Mayfield left the Tampa Bay Buccaneers ' loss to the Minnesota Vikings on Sunday, September 27 with a dislocated right thumb, leaving the quarterback's status uncertain as the team prepares for Week 4.

Mayfield suffered the injury late in Sunday's 23-16 defeat when his throwing hand struck Vikings linebacker Blake Cashman whilst he attempted a pass under pressure as the ball was intercepted by Andrew Van Ginkel .

Mayfield immediately went down holding his hand before eventually leaving the game, the Buccaneers head coach Todd Bowle s confirmed after the game that he had dislocated his right thumb, although Initial X-rays did not reveal a fracture.

Still, an MRI is scheduled for Monday to determine the extent of the injury after the incident came on 31-year-old's final play of the afternoon, forcing rookie Jalon Daniels onto the field for Tampa Bay 's last possession.

Daniels attempted three passes, including an interception on the final play, as the Buccaneers ' comeback hopes disappeared. Mayfield finished 17-of-34 for 217 yards, one touchdown and one interception before leaving.

Buccaneers face uncertainty after another frustrating loss

The injury overshadowed another difficult offensive performance from Tampa Bay as the Buccaneers struggled throughout the afternoon against a Minnesota defense that repeatedly pressured Mayfield and prevented the offense from sustaining drives.

Tampa Bay did produce several opportunities, but penalties and stalled possessions repeatedly prevented the team from turning them into touchdowns whilst their veteran quarterback also took six sacks before his departure.

Mayfield 's potential absence would leave Daniels in line for an expanded role after the undrafted quarterback replaced him against Minnesota . Veteran Easton Stick is currently on Tampa Bay 's practice squad.

Tampa Bay will host the Green Bay Packers in Week 4, but Mayfield 's availability will depend on what the MRI reveals. Bowles ' confirmation of the dislocation provides the first clear indication of the injury, while the imaging will determine whether the quarterback can return quickly or faces an extended absence.

The Buccaneers also lost wide receiver Jalen McMillan to a left knee injury, with an MRI expected to provide further information. Tampa Bay therefore enters the new week dealing with multiple injury concerns while searching for its first victory of the season.

The Vikings are 3-0 and will aim to keep the momentum going on Sunday, October 4 against a Miami Dolphins team that tested the Kansas City Chiefs , eventually losing 24-10 at the Hard Rock Stadium .

articles.title: Who is Starkey Daniels, the mother of Jalon Daniels, who went viral during the Buccaneers' victory in Dallas?
articles.standfirst: The Tampa Bay quarterback’s mother became an unexpected talking point during Thursday Night Football
articles.summary: The Tampa Bay quarterback’s mother became an unexpected talking point during Thursday Night Football
articles.body:
S tarkey Daniels found herself in the spotlight for an unexpected reason during the Tampa Bay Buccaneers ’ 24-16 victory over the Dallas Cowboys on Thursday, October 8.

While her son Jalon Daniels was making headlines for helping Tampa Bay secure its first win of the 2026 NFL season, cameras from the Amazon Prime Video broadcast focused on his mother as she enthusiastically ate nachos in the stands.

The close-up quickly became a talking point on social media, with some fans questioning why the broadcast had lingered on her while she was eating.

One viewer asked, “Now why in the hell is Amazon Prime showing and embarrassing Jalon Daniels ’ mom like that? 🙄” Another fan wrote, “They just did Jalon Daniels’ mom so wrong 😭”

Others joined in, with South Carolina reporter Hale McGranahan writing, “Amazon needs to just let Jalon Daniels ’ mom eat her nachos in peace.” The moment divided attention between the unusual camera shot and the growing excitement surrounding the Buccaneers’ rookie quarterback.

But the broadcast also produced a much warmer scene after the final whistle. When Daniels appeared for his postgame interview, he spotted his mother nearby and invited her to join him.

The moment transformed the viral conversation from one about an awkward camera angle into a celebration of a mother watching her son achieve a major career milestone.

“It’s indescribable. This moment is so big. I’m speechless. I’m so proud of you. I am so proud of you. This is amazing,” Starkey said while sharing the moment with her son.

For Starkey, the victory represented far more than an unexpected result on a Thursday night. Her son had spent years working toward a professional football opportunity, and after going undrafted in 2026, he was now helping an NFL team win a game on one of the league’s biggest weekly stages.

Starkey Daniels’ role in her son’s rise from Kansas to the NFL

Jalon Daniels was born on October 29, 2002, in Lawndale, California. His football development began at Lawndale High School, where he established himself as a promising quarterback before committing to the University of Kansas.

Behind that progression was a family that supported his ambitions long before he became a recognizable name in college football.

Starkey raised Jalon largely on her own during his childhood. A profile published by the Los Angeles Times described how she worked to ensure that the absence of his biological father would not define her son’s upbringing.

She encouraged him to pursue football and helped him navigate a recruiting process that can be difficult for young athletes without established connections.

Jalon has spoken about how he and his mother initially had little understanding of the college recruiting system. As he developed, they learned that talent alone did not always guarantee attention from major programs.

His eventual opportunity at Kansas was the result of sustained work, perseverance and the support of people who believed in his potential.

Starkey later married Tyrone Dubois-Daniels in 2015. Tyrone became an important presence in Jalon’s life, supporting his development alongside Starkey.

Public profiles identify him as Jalon’s stepfather, while the family is also reported to include Jalon’s stepsisters Tylynne, TyLeigh and Tyleri . Kansas’ official athletics profile confirms that Jalon is the son of Starkey and Tyrone Daniels .

The family’s commitment was evident during Jalon’s college career. According to reporting by The Kansas City Star, Starkey and Tyrone made a point of attending his games, with a large group of relatives often gathering to support him. Their presence became part of the quarterback’s experience at Kansas, where he developed into one of the program’s most recognizable players.

Jalon Daniels’ football journey reaches a new milestone in Dallas

Daniels ’ path to the NFL was not straightforward. He joined Kansas in 2020 and gradually established himself as the Jayhawks ’ leading quarterback.

His breakthrough came in 2022, when he threw for 2,014 yards and 18 touchdowns while adding 425 rushing yards and seven rushing touchdowns. His performances earned him second-team All-Big 12 recognition.

Injuries affected his progress, particularly in 2023, but Daniels returned to produce strong seasons in 2024 and 2025. He finished his college career with 9,282 passing yards and 67 touchdown passes, along with 1,445 rushing yards and 23 rushing touchdowns across 49 appearances.

He also excelled academically, graduating with a degree in sport management and earning recognition as a National Football Foundation Scholar-Athlete.

Despite that record, Daniels went undrafted before signing with Tampa Bay as a college free agent in May 2026. He initially joined the Buccaneers as a young quarterback trying to establish himself, but an injury to Baker Mayfield created an opportunity to step into the starting role.

Against Dallas, Daniels completed 19 of 25 passes for 189 yards and a touchdown without throwing an interception.

His composure helped Tampa Bay claim a 24-16 win, while running back Bucky Irving supplied 165 rushing yards and two touchdowns. The victory was the Buccaneers’ first of the season and gave Daniels his first NFL win.

For Starkey , the night was a culmination of years of support and sacrifice. The nacho-eating clip may have made her a viral figure, but the postgame exchange with her son gave viewers a glimpse of what the occasion meant to the family.

Her response was heartfelt, and Daniels ’ decision to bring her into the interview showed that he wanted to share the moment rather than celebrate alone.

In a sport where professional careers can hinge on one opportunity, his victory in Dallas was a significant achievement for a player who had taken the long route to the NFL.

Starkey Daniels may not have expected to become part of the national conversation during Thursday Night Football.

But the viral moment ultimately offered something more meaningful than a joke about a broadcast camera: a reminder of the family support behind a young quarterback’s rise and the emotion that can accompany a long-awaited breakthrough.
